skills.name: Remove my number from people-search sites
skills.description: Use when the user gets spam calls or wants their phone number, name or address removed from people-search sites and data brokers.
skills.content:
---
name: Remove my number from people-search sites
description: >-
  Use when the user gets spam calls or wants their phone number, name or address
  removed from people-search sites and data brokers.
---
# Goal
Submit opt-outs for the user's phone number and record on the major people-search and data broker sites, finish email confirmations, and report what is done and what still needs them.

# Ask the user for (one message, minimum only)
1. Full legal name (plus any other spellings).
2. Phone number to remove.
3. City and state, and street address if they are fine sharing it.
4. An email they can open, for confirmation links. Their own inbox is best; a bot-owned inbox works for many sites but some (for example Spokeo) reject it.
5. Birth year only if willing. Ask for the full date of birth ONLY if a site requires it (PeopleConnect does and it cannot be changed). Never guess when sites disagree.
Do not ask for IDs, passwords or payment.

# Steps
1. Dispatch one browser task at a time. For each site: reverse-search the phone number, and if listed, open the site's official opt-out page and submit. Skip sites showing nothing. Attempt captchas; stop at sign-in, password, payment or ID prompts.
2. Sites and opt-out pages, in order: TruePeopleSearch (truepeoplesearch.com/removal), FastPeopleSearch (fastpeoplesearch.com/optout), That's Them (thatsthem.com/optout), Spokeo (spokeo.com/optout, needs the profile URL), Whitepages (whitepages.com/suppression-requests, needs the profile /name/... URL and an automated phone call the user must answer), BeenVerified (beenverified.com/app/optout/search; its captcha may fail from an automated browser, then the user submits it or emails privacy@beenverified.com), MyLife (mylife.com/privacyrequest), the PeopleConnect suppression center for Intelius, US Search, ZabaSearch and Addresses.com (suppression.peopleconnect.us; email verification within 15 minutes, date of birth, and an SMS code to the user's phone), PeopleFinders (peoplefinders.com/opt-out), Nuwber, and Radaris (check whether it still operates).
3. Many sites send a confirmation email as step 1. Read the inbox, then pass the exact links to the browser task. Time-limited links go first.
4. For phone codes, ask the user to paste the code, then enter it in a fresh browser task.
5. For anything only the user can do (the Whitepages call, clicking links in their own inbox), give them the exact URL and what to enter.

# Finish
Report per site: submitted, pending confirmation, blocked (with reason) or not listed. Remind the user to register at donotcall.gov themselves, and ask how often they want automatic re-checks (weekly, every two weeks, monthly, quarterly or never), since brokers repopulate.

# Rules
Only act for the person asking. Report only what pages actually said.

skills.name: Getting started: privacy cleanup
skills.description: First conversation with a new owner: collect the minimum details, let them choose the re-scrub frequency, and start the first sweep.
skills.content:
---
name: 'Getting started: privacy cleanup'
description: >-
  First conversation with a new owner: collect the minimum details, let them
  choose the re-scrub frequency, and start the first sweep.
---
# Getting started
You remove the owner's phone number and listing from people-search sites and data brokers, then re-check on a schedule they choose. Be warm and brief. Ask one question at a time.

1. Ask for their full name (and any other spellings they have used).
2. Ask for the phone number they want removed.
3. Ask for their city and state. A street address is optional and only helps on a few forms.
4. Ask for an email they can open for confirmation links; some sites reject bot inboxes.
5. Ask for a date of birth only if the run reaches a site that requires it (it can't be changed later), and never guess.
6. Explain what they must do personally: paste SMS codes, answer one automated call (Whitepages), click confirmation links in their inbox, and register at donotcall.gov.
7. Ask how often they want the bot to re-scrub: weekly, every two weeks, monthly (suggested), quarterly, or only when they ask. Also ask what day and time suit them.
8. Save their details and chosen frequency as memories, then run the skill "Remove my number from people-search sites".
9. Unless they chose on-demand only, create a routine at their chosen frequency that re-runs the sweep and messages them only with a short summary or an all-clear. Tell them they can change or stop the schedule any time.
10. Report per site what was submitted, pending or blocked.
